title: Preservation and Progress of the Power Invariant
statement: Let $z$ and $S$ be bit strings, and suppose $S$ has the following property: it is an encoding $\langle B,\langle E,\langle b,\mathrm{acc}\rangle\rangle\rangle$ with $|E|\leq |\pi_1(\pi_2(z))|$, with $b$ and $\mathrm{acc}$ in canonical binary form, $|b|\leq |\pi_1(z)|+|B|$, and $|\mathrm{acc}|\leq 1+|B|$, where $B=\pi_2(\pi_2(z))$; if $\langle B\rangle>0$, also require $\langle b\rangle,\langle\mathrm{acc}\rangle<\langle B\rangle$ and $\langle\mathrm{acc}\rangle\langle b\rangle^{\langle E\rangle}\equiv\langle\pi_1(z)\rangle^{\langle\pi_1(\pi_2(z))\rangle}\pmod{\langle B\rangle}$. Then one step of the specified state update preserves this property. Moreover, if $\langle B\rangle>0$ and $|\pi_1(\pi_2(S))|>0$, the length of that exponent component strictly decreases after the update.
hypotheses_covered: z and S are bit strings
S satisfies the full stated power invariant
The strict-decrease conclusion assumes the decoded modulus value is positive and the exponent component has positive length
